title: Section 134 — Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person

content.overview: BNS s. 134 — Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person. BNS restatement of IPC 356. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 356. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 134 is the rule on “Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person”. The section provides that whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting to commit theft on any property which that person is then wearing or carrying, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 134 exists so that “Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail

learningObjectives: Master the offence of assault or criminal force in attempting theft under BNS s. 134.
Analyze the requirement that the property must be worn or carried by the person.
Examine the two-year imprisonment tier, fine, or both.
Understand the relationship between Section 134, snatching (s. 304), and robbery (s. 307).
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 134 penalizes whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting to commit theft on any property which that person is then wearing or carrying, with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes physical force and threats used during attempted street theft targeting property carried or worn on a person's body.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 134 (corresponding to IPC s. 356).
Actus reus: Assaulting (s. 130) or using criminal force (s. 129).
Context: In attempting to commit theft on any property.
Location of property: Property which the victim is then wearing or carrying.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to two years, or fine, or both.
essentialIngredients: The victim was wearing or carrying property.
The accused attempted to commit theft of that property.
In attempting such theft, the accused assaulted or used criminal force against the victim.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 134 carries forward IPC 356, targeting street pickpocketing, bag-snatching attempts, and thefts from the person where physical force or threats are employed. The property must be physically worn (such as a necklace, wristwatch, or jacket) or carried (such as a handbag, backpack, or umbrella) by the victim at the time of the attempt. The offence does not require that the theft be successfully completed; using force or an assaultive gesture while trying to steal the carried item completes the crime under Section 134. If actual fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint is caused to effect the theft, the crime ascends to robbery under Section 307.
examples: Teaching example (Attempted chain snatching): An accused runs up behind a pedestrian, reaches for her gold necklace, and violently tugs it; the chain snags on her collar and fails to break, but the force wrenches her neck. The accused is guilty under s. 134.

Teaching example (Grabbing a handbag): An accused attempts to wrest a handbag from a commuter's shoulder on a train platform, struggling with her until bystanders intervene. This is an offence under s. 134.
distinctions: Section 134 vs Robbery (s. 307): Section 134 penalizes using force in attempting theft from a person (up to 2 years); Robbery requires causing or attempting death, hurt, or wrongful restraint to effect the theft (up to 10 or 14 years).
Section 134 vs Simple Theft (s. 303): Simple theft involves stealthy taking without force; Section 134 requires an assault or use of criminal force.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who lunged at a pedestrian, grabbed the strap of her laptop bag, and pulled hard before fleeing when she screamed, committed an offence under s. 134.
Rule: Using criminal force in attempting to commit theft of property carried by a person satisfies BNS s. 134.
Application: The bag was carried by the person, force was used to attempt theft, and the attempt was proven.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 134.

keyTakeaways: Penalizes assault or criminal force in attempting theft from a person.
Property must be worn or carried by the victim at that moment.
Completed upon using force in the attempt; successful theft is not required.
Punishable with up to two years imprisonment, fine, or both.
